_: THE vocabulary, once. Python (funnel.py), the work rail (funnelPile.js) and the Timeline (timelineState.js) all build their tables from this file, so a word cannot mean one thing on the rail, another in chat and a third on the Timeline. Three groups by PURPOSE, not three vocabularies: `lanes` is what is happening to a piece of live work (it also carries the funnel's ordering, so nothing may be added here that is not live work); `kinds` overrides a lane where the lane is not enough; `states` is what the Timeline says about a row that is no longer live work. A word lives in exactly one of them. `counted` is the plural-counting form for prose and defaults to `word`.

lanes.hint: an agent stopped and is waiting on you — it is blocking work
lanes._says: the ONE sentence each sub-state of this lane gets, on every surface (workerstate.says / funnelPile.says). `line` when the request has words, `bare` when it does not. asking = a question, approval = a permission, stalled = a turn that died on a wall (rate limit, token ceiling) with the CLI alive at its prompt, parked = quiet at its prompt with nothing recorded

parked.bare: {agent} stopped and is waiting on you

lanes.hint: a meeting inside two hours, or an urgent sender
a reply or an action is drafted and waits for your yes
a person asked you for something and nobody is on it
real work with nobody on it - do it yourself, or send it to an agent
handed to an agent and not started yet

a report or workflow you set up could not run - the cause is in it
triage could not classify this — nothing was started; open it and retry, or choose what it is
the ask that slipped, the promise you made, the thread gone quiet
a report you set up landed, or an agent finished a job
a person told you something — read it or don't
an agent has it — nothing for you until it stops or asks; it moves up when it needs your input
